clue.text: Stop and beg for silk fabric

parts.note: to dam a river is to stop its flow
to beg is to ask earnestly

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop pleading for a length of silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a reversible patterned woven cloth, traditionally made of silk, named after Damascus.

clue.text: Palace supporter backing a loser originally, bad player

indicators.note: to back something is to stand behind it, so this piece comes after the rest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what something was originally is how it began, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of loser
a ham is an overacting, poor actor
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A Crystal Palace fan backs a struggling side while lamenting one poor performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palace' suggests the football club, but it is the definition: the Moorish palace in Granada. The supporter sits behind the other three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the famous Moorish palace and fortress complex in Granada, southern Spain.

clue.text: I kneel when playing with brat, little kid

indicators.note: the letters are played with, rearranged freely like toys

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent gets down on their knees to play with a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankle-biter is informal slang for a small child, one short enough to nip at your ankles.

clue.text: Hater furious about erection of house, jointly owned property

indicators.note: in a down clue, erecting a word stands it up so it reads from bottom to top
about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
a furious person is in turmoil, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters of hater, rearranged
a semi is a semi-detached house, one sharing a wall with its neighbour

explanation.surface: An angry objector protests at a new house going up on shared land.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house, a common British suburban home. 'Erection' suits a building going up, but in a down clue it turns the word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A timeshare is a holiday property whose ownership is split among several people, each using it for set weeks.

clue.text: Fabric cut for muppet

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: cloth is woven fabric

explanation.surface: Material is trimmed to make a Muppet puppet.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital M in Muppet is hidden by the clue's opening; 'muppet' is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Clot and muppet are both mild British insults for a stupid or clumsy person.

clue.text: Rodent with disease in pain, shaved

indicators.note: in places the illness inside the trimmed word
shaving takes off the edges, so only the inner letters survive

parts.note: pain with its first and last letters removed
gout is a disease causing painful swollen joints

explanation.surface: A rodent, suffering illness and pain, has had its fur shaved.
explanation.definitionFit: An agouti is a long-legged South American rodent related to the guinea pig.

clue.text: Learner in various courses finishing actions

indicators.note: in places the learner among the other letters
various suggests different forms, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student takes several courses on how to finish things.
explanation.definitionFit: Closures are acts of closing or bringing something to an end, which are finishing actions.

clue.text: Social worker opens maps, briefly, in state capital

indicators.note: the worker opens up the other word and goes inside it
briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps
ants live in organised colonies, social insects that work

explanation.surface: A social worker consults maps in a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a caseworker, but it is an insect: ants are social and famously industrious.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital city of the US state of Georgia.

clue.text: Youth order awarded since bullying offensive, first of all

indicators.note: first of all means the leading letter of every word that follows

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A youngster was given a court order because their bullying was offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO (Anti-Social Behaviour Order) was a British court order, often given to young troublemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: The ASBO was a civil order restricting antisocial behaviour, notoriously associated with teenagers in Britain.

clue.text: Criminal, could one be as sick as a parrot, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the answer is how the phrase is spoken

parts.words: could one be as sick as a parrot
parts.note: a poorly bird of prey, sick as a parrot is

explanation.surface: Asks whether a lawbreaker might feel thoroughly miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick as a parrot' is British slang for bitterly disappointed; here a bird that is unwell could be an ill eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal and illegal are adjective synonyms describing an act that breaks the law.

clue.text: A deep depression surrounds island that's back up for grabs

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: surrounds puts the depression around the other piece

parts.note: a vale is a valley

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the island's name is read right to left

parts.note: Bali is an Indonesian island

explanation.surface: A deep low-pressure weather system circles an island and is set to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back up' looks like a phrase, but 'back' reverses and 'up' begins the definition 'up for grabs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up for grabs is free for anyone to take, which is what available means.

clue.text: Baskets, small vessels filled with runners, initially

indicators.note: filled with means the vessels hold the other letter inside

parts.note: tugs are small boats that tow ships

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter of runners

explanation.surface: Baskets and small boats are loaded with runner beans.
explanation.walkthrough: A trug is a shallow British garden basket made of wooden strips.
explanation.definitionFit: Trugs are shallow oval baskets used by gardeners for carrying produce and flowers.

clue.text: Takeaway dish with honey and milk ultimately rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: honey and babe are both terms of endearment

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of milk

explanation.surface: A takeaway meal comes with honey, but the milk is sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab is a dish of grilled meat, a staple bought from takeaway shops.

clue.text: Not right there, if carrying more weight

indicators.note: something not right is wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something isn't quite right if you're heavier than you should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' tempts you to drop an R; nothing is removed, as all seven letters are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Heftier is the comparative of hefty, meaning bulkier or heavier than something else.

clue.text: Nearly sixteen strong

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: four multiplied by itself is sixteen

explanation.surface: Someone almost sixteen years old is robust.
explanation.definitionFit: Foursquare means solidly based and firm, so a steady, strong structure or stance.

clue.text: Smell, one drifting around old fish

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters wrap about the extra letter
drifting letters float out of place and settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A whiff drifts around an old fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is a European flatfish prized for eating, a particular kind of fish.

clue.text: Foxes' home surrounded by water, cockerels perhaps rule the roost

indicators.note: surrounded by means the den sits inside the other word

parts.note: to water something is to wet it
a fox's burrow is called an earth
cockerels wake people at dawn, so they are rousers

explanation.surface: Foxes live by water while cockerels dominate the farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rule the roost' fits the cockerels so well it seems part of the picture, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear the trousers is an idiom for being the one in charge of a household, as is ruling the roost.

clue.text: Artist, one with small instrument?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American painter James McNeill ...
second meaning: someone who plays a tin whistle, a small wind instrument

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a painter is someone carrying a tiny instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler painted the famous portrait of his mother, and anyone playing a whistle is also a whistler.

clue.text: Vision okay in crew

indicators.note: in places the word of assent inside the crew

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes is a word of agreement, like okay

explanation.surface: A rowing crew's eyesight is passed as acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision and eyesight are synonyms for the faculty of seeing.

clue.text: Blazer on umpire returned after batting

indicators.note: after means this part comes later, following the batting piece

parts.note: a cricketer batting is in

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so these words are read from right to left

parts.note: a ref (referee) is an umpire

explanation.surface: An umpire's blazer is put back on after a cricketer's innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blazer' looks like a jacket, which suits the cricket scene; here it means something that blazes.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a large uncontrolled fire, something that blazes fiercely.

clue.text: Light seed transported by jet

indicators.note: something transported by a vehicle is carried inside it

parts.note: to jet somewhere is to fly
an oat is a cereal grain, a seed

explanation.surface: A light seed is carried along by an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Floaty describes something light and airy, such as a delicate dress fabric.

clue.text: Promise Cornish maize?

parts.note: Cornwall lies in the south-west of England
an ear is the seed-bearing head of a cereal such as maize

explanation.surface: Asks whether there is a pledge involving corn grown in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-western tip, so Cornish gives SW.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to promise solemnly, as when taking an oath.

clue.text: Look at care

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to gaze at or consider

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to look at steadily, and the noun means attention or consideration for others.

clue.text: Steal game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to copy someone else's work
second meaning: short for cribbage, a card game

explanation.definitionFit: To crib is to plagiarise or pilfer, and crib is the usual short name for the card game cribbage.

clue.text: Supernatural being in middle of earth wearing ring

indicators.note: the ring wears this letter, holding it inside like clothing

parts.note: a bell's ring is a toll

indicators.note: middle of keeps only the central letter of the following word

parts.note: the central letter of earth

explanation.surface: A mythical being in Middle-earth wears a magic ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Tolkien's Middle-earth and the One Ring; here 'middle of' simply selects a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is a creature of Scandinavian folklore, a supernatural giant or dwarf.

clue.text: Peer into barrel or drum

indicators.note: into suggests looking inside the following words for the answer

parts.note: spans the end of barrel, all of or and the start of drum

explanation.surface: Someone looks inside a barrel or a drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' reads as a verb meaning look, but it is the noun: a member of the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord is a peer, a member of the British nobility entitled to sit in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Development announced in April or May, say?

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the season

parts.note: April and May are spring months
news that is out has been made public

explanation.surface: Some development is announced in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Announced' looks like a homophone signal, but it means made public.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprouting is growth or development, as of shoots from a seed.

clue.text: Rivet then broken, one pulled from track

indicators.note: broken letters are smashed apart and reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: pulled from means taken out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a rail is a track for trains
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rivet breaks and part of a railway line is torn away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rivet' looks like a metal fastener but is the verb meaning to hold someone's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to captivate, and to rivet someone is likewise to hold their attention completely.

clue.text: Patty dictated for old citizen

indicators.note: something dictated is spoken out for writing down, so the sound matters

parts.note: a patty is a flat round cake of minced meat

explanation.surface: A meat patty is ordered for an elderly townsperson.
explanation.definitionFit: A burgher was a citizen of a town or borough, an archaic term, hence old.
